Campus crime: Underage drinking and larceny reported at UNC this week

This is The Daily Tar Heel’s weekly campus crime brief, in which senior writer AnnaJames Lynch summarizes the crimes reported on campus in the last seven days, every Sunday.
AnnaJames Lynch, Senior Writer • August 23, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:51
Instaread
Nidhi Philar

Underage alcohol consumption, suspicious conditions and larceny were all reported at UNC within the past week, from Sunday, Aug. 16, to Saturday, Aug. 22. 

These incidents were reported in the UNC Police Crime Log to comply with the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act, or Clery Act. All American colleges and universities participating in federal financial aid programs, including UNC System schools, comply with the federal law. It requires timely warnings of crimes and offenses that present a threat to the safety of students or employees, as well as the publication of campus security policies. 

Though publicly available in police reports, The DTH does not name those reported committing nonviolent crimes, such as alcohol violations, to avoid unnecessary harm. The DTH also excludes well-being checks.

Here are the campus crimes reported within the last week:

Sunday, Aug. 16

  • An individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 12:55 a.m. at Parker Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.
  • An individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 1:10 a.m. at Granville Towers East. This case is now inactive.
  • Another individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 1:29 a.m. at Granville Towers East. This case is now inactive.

Monday, Aug. 17

  • A suspicious non-criminal condition , which is an incident out of the ordinary but not related to criminal activity, was reported to have occurred at 2:01 p.m. on Aug. 7 at the Genetic Medicine Building. This case is still open.
  • Property damage (non-criminal) was reported to have occurred at 6:23 p.m. at the UNC Cogeneration Facility. This case is now inactive.
  • Underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 10 p.m. at Thomas Ruffin Jr. Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.
  • Another instance of underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 11 p.m. at Thomas Ruffin Jr. Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.

Tuesday, Aug. 18

  • A suspicious condition (criminal), which is an incident out of the ordinary that is related to a criminal activity, was reported to have occurred at midnight on Aug. 15 at the Public Safety Building. This case is still open.
  • An individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 9:55 a.m. at Phillips Hall. This case is now inactive.
  • Larceny from a building was reported to have occurred at 3:30 p.m. at the FedEx Global Education Center. This case is still open.
  • Underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 11 p.m. at Ehringhaus Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.
  • Another instance of underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 11 p.m. at Ehringhaus Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.

Wednesday, Aug. 19

  • Underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 12:20 a.m. at Cobb Residence Hall. This case is now inactive.
  • An individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 3:10 a.m. at Ehringhaus Residence Hall. This case is still open.
  • A warning of trespass and a suspicious condition (non-criminal) were reported at 5:49 p.m. at the Tate-Turner-Kuralt Building. This case is now inactive. 

Thursday, Aug.  20

  • A suspicious condition (non-criminal) was reported to have occurred at 3:30 p.m. at the Genome Sciences Building. This case is still open.
  • Larceny was reported to have occurred at 7:15 a.m. at Lenoir Dining Hall. This case is still open.

Friday, Aug. 21

  • No crimes were reported on this day.

Saturday, Aug. 22

  • Underage alcohol consumption was reported to have occurred at 11:15 p.m. at Morrison Residence Hall. This case is still open.
  • An individual was reported to have consumed tax-paid liquor at 11:21 p.m. at Manly Residence Hall. This case is still open.

The DTH obtains incident reports and outlines related details when possible, but some of these circumstantial details are excluded from public copies. The DTH will follow up on some incidents in subsequent reporting to provide more information.
